preamble: No direct shift of the postalveolar fricative [ʃ] to the uvular fricative [χ] is documented. The case usually cited, the Spanish readjustment of sibilants, retracted merged Old Spanish /ʃ/ to velar /x/ around the 16th–17th centuries; the uvular [χ] heard for the jota in central and northern Spain is a later, regional realization of that /x/. The development is therefore a two-step chain (ʃ > x, then x > [χ]) and belongs in the cells sh_to_x and x_to_x_uvular.

examples.note: The documented change was ʃ > velar x; the uvular realization is a later regional variant of /x/, not a direct outcome of /ʃ/.

sources: Penny, R. (2002). A History of the Spanish Language (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511992827
Hualde, J. I. (2005). The Sounds of Spanish. Cambridge University Press.
